q: My listed buyer has issued a green bond. What will it ask me as an MSME supplier?
title: Your listed buyer issued a green bond
short: Expect requests for energy, fuel, emissions and waste figures. A green bond issuer reports project impact and BRSR items, including Scope 3 and the share of suppliers assessed, and must avoid cherry-picked data. Its ESG rating also counts MSME sourcing, so documented data helps you stay on its list.

sections.h: Why the request lands on you
ul: SEBI requires listed green debt issuers to report major BRSR items, including total Scope 3 emissions and the percentage of value chain partners, by value of business, assessed for environmental impact.
Impact must be reported project by project, with methods and assumptions, and negative externalities quantified.
SEBI's greenwashing rules forbid cherry-picking data, so buyers need numbers that hold up rather than estimates.

sections.h: What is likely to be asked
ol: Monthly electricity use in kWh and fuel use by type, with bills or invoices.
Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, or the data to calculate them.
Waste generated, recycled and disposed of, and water withdrawn.
Whether any figure was checked by an outside party.
For supplies to a funded project, the materials and transport behind your product.

p: SEBI's list of India-specific ESG rating parameters includes the share of a company's inputs bought directly from MSMEs and small producers. ESG mutual funds must hold mostly companies with assured BRSR Core data. A supplier that answers quickly with traceable figures makes its buyer's reporting easier, which is a practical edge when contracts are renewed.

ul: Keep 12 months of electricity bills and fuel invoices in one place.
Use one method and state the emission factors you used.
Answer only what you can support; mark estimates as estimates.

senseible: Senseible reads a supplier's electricity bills and fuel invoices into Scope 1 and 2 figures with the source document attached, ready to share with a buyer.
